name: Todd Creek

facts.strongest_angle:
LEAD WITH: the acre, the slope and the shale — NOT with saving water.

This is the one town in the batch where the standard water-savings pitch is actively weak, because the Todd Creek Village Metropolitan District runs a dual-pipe system and, as of March 5, 2026, every TCVMD-served property can irrigate with NON-POTABLE water. A Todd Creek homeowner is not lying awake over their irrigation bill. Any competitor who opens with "stop watering your lawn" tells this audience they have never worked here.

Instead, lead with: "An acre of Renohill clay on a 3 to 9 percent grade is the reason your backyard green has to be engineered, not rolled out." Then the practice-green offer: a real multi-hole putting and chipping complex on an acre lot, five minutes from an Arthur Hills championship layout (Todd Creek Golf Club, 7,435 yards) and from Pete Dye's Riverdale Dunes, Colorado's top-ranked public course. Median household income here is $194,362 with a 0.5% poverty rate and 98.2% owner-occupancy — this audience buys the engineered answer and buys it once.

WHY THIS DIFFERS FROM ITS NEIGHBOURS:
- vs HENDERSON, its nearest neighbour to the south: Henderson sits on flat Vona sandy loam at 0-1% slope and much of it pumps from private wells, so Henderson's page IS a water page and a mud/dust page. Todd Creek's is a grade-and-heave page and a golf page. Same county, opposite arguments.
- vs TWIN LAKES / SHAW HEIGHTS: smectitic Platner loam on 0-3% and 3-5%, quarter-acre and smaller lots, half the income. Todd Creek is montmorillonitic shale-derived clay on up to 9%, acreage lots, double the income.
- vs anything in Thornton proper: the CDP is unincorporated with no city permit, while the annexed Heritage side needs a Thornton Minor Development Permit.

SECONDARY HOOKS, in order:
1. THE ANNEXATION SPLIT AS PROOF OF EXPERTISE. Say it out loud: Heritage Todd Creek (8455 Heritage Dr) is inside Thornton city limits, the rest of Todd Creek is unincorporated Adams County, and the rules are completely different. Then deliver on it.
2. THE $2/SQ FT THORNTON REBATE. For the Thornton-side homes, Thornton Water pays up to $2 per square foot on 200-1,000 sq ft artificial turf projects, lifetime cap $2,000 per lot. Offer to handle the whole submittal — the design, the W-9, the material receipts for sub-base, turf, seaming and infill, and the before/during/after photos, which are all mandatory. Almost no competitor will do this paperwork.
3. PFAS-FREE AS A DIFFERENTIATOR. Thornton's rules require PFAS-free turf and infill, explicitly reject "PFC-free" wording, and explicitly reject the manufacturer's own testing. Stocking and documenting a genuinely PFAS-free product is a moat, and it also reassures the acreage families with kids and dogs on the unincorporated side who have no permit requirement at all.
4. STAGE 1 DROUGHT ON THE THORNTON SIDE. Two days a week since March 15, 2026, nothing between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m., fines from $100 after a 10-day cure period, and new sod only permitted in May, June, September and October on a 21-day permit. That last detail is a great closing line: a real lawn is now on a government schedule; a synthetic one is not.
5. THE 55+ ANGLE. Heritage Todd Creek's 1,300 homes are age-restricted; "never mow again" lands differently at 68 than at 38, and the paired homes already include front landscaping so the sale is the back yard.

CANNIBALISATION WARNING: 80602 and the Brighton/Weld fringe are the most likely place in this batch for Timeless Grass & Greens to collide with the owner's NoCo Turf Co. town pages. Todd Creek should be written for the Denver-metro brand with the golf and acreage framing above, and the two sites should not both target "artificial turf Brighton CO."
facts.ordinance_or_hoa:
THE KEY POINT: which rulebook applies depends on which side of the annexation line the house sits, and almost no competitor will get this right.

A) UNINCORPORATED TODD CREEK CDP — no city permit. Subject to Adams County regulation only, plus subdivision covenants and metropolitan district rules. HONEST LIMITATION: I could not verify whether the Adams County Development Standards and Regulations contain any artificial-turf provision; the code sits on adamscounty.municipalcodeonline.com, a JavaScript-only platform I could not search, and the county's own site search is client-side. Confirm with Adams County Community & Economic Development, 720.523.6800 / cedd-plan@adamscountyco.gov before publishing any claim that there are no county rules.

B) THORNTON-ANNEXED TODD CREEK (including Heritage Todd Creek at 8455 Heritage Dr, and 152nd & Holly, and 16000 Elizabeth St) — a detailed and demanding artificial-turf code applies, and a competent installer who knows it wins the job. Verbatim from Thornton Water's 2026 Artificial Turf Rules (dated 1/1/2026), which reproduces Figure 452.1 of the Thornton City Code:
- A MINOR DEVELOPMENT PERMIT is required BEFORE installation of artificial turf as landscaping (Planner of the Day, POD.info@thorntonco.gov, 303-538-7295).
- Rear yards and enclosed side yards: "Artificial turf allowed with no limitations." All other areas (front and unenclosed side yards not occupied by driveways, sidewalks, patios, decks, buildings or structures): "Artificial turf shall not exceed 25% of the landscape area."
- Turf must be installed and maintained to "simulate the appearance of a well-maintained lawn effectively," must be a green colour like natural grass, and must carry a MINIMUM EIGHT-YEAR WARRANTY AGAINST FADING.
- BUFFERS: 3 ft from all property lines (turf may reach the front property line if a 3 ft buffer sits between turf and the street sidewalk); 8 ft from the front wall of any building and 3 ft from all other building walls or impervious surfaces when outside the rear or enclosed side yard; 3 ft from any deciduous tree trunk and no closer than the dripline of any evergreen. Buffers must be permeable — wood mulch, gravel or rock max 2 inches diameter.
- LIVING PLANTS REQUIRED in front or unenclosed side yards: one tree equivalent for the first 750 sq ft of turf or fraction thereof, plus half a tree equivalent for each additional 250 sq ft. One tree equivalent = one 2-inch deciduous tree, or one 6-ft evergreen, or 10 #5 shrubs, or 20 #1 ornamental grasses.
- MATERIALS: cut-pile infill type; polypropylene, biobased, nylon, polyester, polyethylene or blends stitched to meshed or hole-punched backing; hole spacing not exceeding 4 in by 6 in on centre; backing must drain at a minimum of TWO INCHES PER HOUR. Indoor/outdoor carpet is expressly not permitted.
- PFAS-FREE REQUIRED for turf, infill and all manufactured install products — and the bar is high: a public manufacturer statement using language such as "PFAS-free" or "fluorocarbon-free" ("PFC-free" is explicitly NOT sufficient), or published independent testing; "Testing completed by the manufacturer does not satisfy this requirement," and third-party certifications do not count unless total organic fluorine is evaluated with public results. Documentation is submitted at permit application.
- INSTALLATION: existing sod/ground cover must be removed first; sub-base minimum 3 inches of compacted aggregate, optionally coarse and fine layers separated by geotextile, and "the specified base material(s) system must contain a minimum of one-half inch of precipitation before generating sheet flow runoff"; anchored at all edges and seams with manufacturer-recommended pins/nails; ALL SEAMS GLUED, NOT SEWN; infill of clean-washed sand and/or ground shells where the manufacturer requires it.
- MAINTENANCE obligations under Thornton Code 18-556: cleaning with biodegradable products, brushing, debris removal, hand raking worn areas, repairing depressions, brushing back displaced infill, eliminating odours, matting, weeds and loose edges, and replacement when maintenance can no longer simulate healthy living turf.

C) HOAs. C.R.S. 38-33.3-106.5(1)(i) means a Colorado association cannot prohibit "the use of xeriscape, nonvegetative turf grass, or drought-tolerant vegetative landscapes," and guidelines must "not prohibit the use of nonvegetative turf grass in the backyard of a unit owner's property." Heritage Todd Creek runs Residential Improvement Guidelines through a Design Review and Compliance process, so a submittal is still required — the association can regulate appearance, it just cannot ban a backyard synthetic lawn. Thornton's own rebate rules also instruct applicants to "Get HOA Approval."

D) SB24-005. From January 1, 2026, no new artificial turf on common interest community property, commercial/institutional/industrial property, or rights-of-way/medians — athletic fields of play excepted. So do not pitch new turf into Heritage Todd Creek's common areas or the metro district's streetscape.
facts.water_and_rules:
THIS IS THE MOST COUNTER-INTUITIVE FINDING IN THE BATCH, AND IT SHOULD CHANGE HOW THE PAGE IS WRITTEN.

PROVIDER 1 — TODD CREEK VILLAGE METROPOLITAN DISTRICT (TCVMD), the main supplier inside the CDP. EPA SDWIS PWSID CO0101157, population served 7,363, 2,727 service connections, primary source code GU (groundwater under the direct influence of surface water) — i.e. it produces its own water rather than buying treated water, unlike every other district in this batch. Office at 10450 E. 159th Court, Brighton CO 80602 (geocoded: Todd Creek CDP). Just over 2,750 residential and commercial accounts today against a planned build-out of 21,024 units.

CRITICALLY: TCVMD runs a DUAL-PIPE SYSTEM delivering both potable water and separate NON-POTABLE IRRIGATION WATER, and its site states that as of MARCH 5, 2026 all TCVMD-served properties have the availability to use non-potable irrigation water.

WHY THAT MATTERS: the standard artificial-turf sales argument — "stop paying to water your lawn" — is measurably WEAKER in Todd Creek than anywhere else in this batch, because irrigation here does not consume expensive treated potable water. If the page leads with water savings, an informed Todd Creek homeowner will dismiss it. The page must lead with something else (see strongest_angle).

PROVIDER 2 — City of Thornton, for the annexed portions including Heritage Todd Creek. EPA PWSID CO0101150, 226,465 people, 42,530 connections, own surface supply. Thornton is currently under STAGE 1 DROUGHT RESTRICTIONS, effective March 15, 2026: "Limit lawn watering to two days/week, at this time Thornton customers can choose their two watering days"; "No lawn watering between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m." Trees, shrubs, perennials, annuals and vegetable gardens may be watered any day. New sod or seed requires a 21-day permit, available in May, June, September and October only. Violations: courtesy warning first; uncorrected leaks or waste after 10 days draw fines starting at $100 residential, $250 commercial, $1,000 construction, escalating on repeats.

PROVIDER 3 — small groundwater systems and private wells at the fringe. RIVERDALE PEAKS II METROPOLITAN DISTRICT (PWSID CO0101675) serves 209 people on 53 connections from groundwater. Some acreage parcels are on individual domestic wells.

DOES ARTIFICIAL TURF QUALIFY FOR A REBATE? Yes — but only on the Thornton side, and this is the single most valuable commercial fact I found in this batch.

THORNTON WATER PAYS FOR ARTIFICIAL TURF. Its Water-Wise Landscape Rebate covers artificial turf under a dedicated rules document ("2026 Artificial Turf Rules for Water-Wise Landscape Rebate"): up to $2 PER SQUARE FOOT for qualifying projects of 200 to 1,000 square feet, with a LIFETIME MAXIMUM OF $2,000 PER RESIDENTIAL LOT. The turf must replace high-water-demand lawn such as Kentucky bluegrass on an existing residential lot, or areas of no landscaping on a new-construction residential lot. Turf on existing hardscape (patios, side-yard concrete, pathways) does NOT qualify. The applicant must submit the design on the Water-Wise Landscape Rebate application, a signed IRS W-9, a copy of their driver's licence, receipts for ALL materials (sub-base, turf, seaming materials, infill), before/during/after photos, and the installer's contact details. HOA approval must be obtained where applicable.

BY CONTRAST, on the HOA/commercial side Thornton states artificial turf DOES NOT qualify for its Commercial & Common Area Water-Wise Landscape Grant, and its page cites Colorado SB24-005, which from January 1, 2026 "Prohibits the installation of nonfunctional turf, artificial turf, and invasive plant species on certain properties."

STATE PROGRAM: the CWCB Turf Replacement Grant Program stopped accepting applications in March 2025 and expects funding exhausted; homeowners and HOAs were never directly eligible.

Also live at check date: unincorporated Adams County is under Stage 1 Fire Restrictions by Sheriff's order.
facts.soil_and_yard:
The hardest ground in the batch, verified from USDA SSURGO via Soil Data Access (point query at 39.9780, -104.8733):

Map unit ReD — RENOHILL LOAM, 3 TO 9 PERCENT SLOPES.
- Renohill, 85%, well drained, taxonomic class "Fine, MONTMORILLONITIC, mesic Ustollic Haplargids"
- Samsil, 5%
- Shingle, 5%
- Terry, 5%

Two things make this materially worse than Twin Lakes or Shaw Heights, and the page should say so in plain language:

1. MONTMORILLONITIC. Montmorillonite is the classic high-activity swelling clay — the Front Range heaving-soil villain. Renohill is a clayey soil formed in material weathered from soft calcareous SHALE, and both of its minor companions (Samsil, Shingle) are shallow shale-derived soils. In practice that means shallow depth to weathered shale bedrock, a stiff clay profile that swells wet and shrinks and cracks dry, and very low infiltration.

2. SLOPE 3 TO 9 PERCENT. That is real fall across an acre lot — the steepest of the five places. Combined with clay that will not take water, you get sheet flow, erosion channels and a base that migrates downhill if it is not built properly.

What that means for the work, and what makes a great technical section on this page:
- A putting green on an acre lot here needs cut-and-fill and a designed subgrade, not a levelling pass. You cannot roll a true green over 3-9% Renohill.
- Full excavation, geotextile separation, a thicker compacted aggregate base than a flat clay site needs, and engineered surface drainage away from foundations — heaving Renohill next to a house is also a structural concern, so the drainage design is a selling point, not a line item.
- Perimeter and toe-of-slope drainage matters because the shale beneath will not accept infiltration.
- Talk about crack-and-heave: homeowners here already know what expansive soil does to their driveways, patios and basement walls. Naming Renohill and montmorillonite by name is credibility.

Elevation 5,036 ft. CDP 9.889 sq mi total, 9.694 land and 0.195 water — the water is the reservoirs and the Todd Creek drainage (Smith Reservoir, Guthrie Reservoir No. 1, Stouffer Reservoir No. 1 all appear in the area).
facts.housing_stock:
CHECK DATE 2026-09-07. This is the affluent, large-lot page — the closest thing in this batch to the "upper echelon" the owner wants.

ACS 2020-2024 (Census Reporter, geoid 16000US0877757), 1,808 housing units, year structure built:
- 1939 or earlier: 15 (old farmsteads)
- 1950-59: 6
- 1960-69: 92
- 1970-79: 20
- 1980-89: 27
- 1990-99: 156
- 2000-09: 1,016  (56% — the defining cohort)
- 2010-19: 455  (25%)
- 2020 or later: 21

So more than four out of five homes were built after 2000. This is 2000s-and-2010s semi-custom and custom production housing, not old farmhouses — despite the rural setting.

Units in structure (B25024): 1,781 single-family detached, 22 in 10-19 unit buildings, 5 mobile homes, and essentially nothing else. There is NO attached product, NO duplex, NO small multifamily.

Tenure (B25003): 1,761 owner-occupied vs 32 renter-occupied. That is 98.2% ownership — the highest in the batch by a wide margin and one of the highest you will find anywhere in metro Denver. Almost every door you knock on is the decision-maker.

Median home value $897,200. Average household size 3.0.

LOT SIZE, DERIVED: the CDP covers 9.694 sq mi of land = 6,204 acres, against 1,808 units. That is 3.4 acres per dwelling gross. Population density is 544 per sq mi. Even allowing for open space, farmland, the Todd Creek drainage and reservoirs, this confirms an acreage-lot community — 1 acre and up is the norm, with pockets larger. Wikipedia records 1,683 units at the 2020 Census with a 2.1% vacancy rate, and 81% of households married-couple, 36.5% with children under 18.

HOA PREVALENCE: high but fragmented — this is not one master HOA, it is a patchwork of subdivision associations and metropolitan districts, with the Todd Creek Village Metropolitan District and a Park and Recreation District named in the CDP's own description.

IMPORTANT BOUNDARY CORRECTION FOR THE PAGE. Heritage Todd Creek — the 1,300-home Lennar 55+ community built 2006-2023, homes low $600,000s to low $1,000,000s, HOA $145-$233/month, paired homes include front landscaping and snow removal to the front door — is NOT in Todd Creek CDP. I geocoded 8455 Heritage Dr and it returns THORNTON CITY. Likewise 16000 Elizabeth St and 152nd & Holly return Thornton city. 9200 E 152nd Ave and 10450 E 159th Ct (the metro district office) return Todd Creek CDP. So "Todd Creek" as a market is split between unincorporated county acreage and Thornton-annexed subdivisions, and the two have DIFFERENT permit and rebate rules. The page must handle both, and the distinction is a credibility win.
facts.who_lives_there:
The money. ACS 2020-2024: population 5,379 (5,028 at the 2020 Census, up 33.4% from 2010).

- MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME $194,362 — more than double the US figure of $80,734, and roughly double Twin Lakes ($95,583) and Shaw Heights ($86,250).
- Per capita income $72,827.
- POVERTY RATE 0.5%. Essentially zero.
- Median age 45.1-45.3.
- Average household size 3.0.
- Education: 94.4% high school or higher, 42.3% bachelor's or higher.
- Median travel time to work 31.7 minutes — a commuter-executive profile, people who buy back their weekends.
- Only 3% moved in the past year — extremely stable, long-hold owners who will pay for something permanent.
- Foreign-born 4%. Veterans 6.7% (282 people). Racially about 79.7% white, 12% multiracial, 15.5% Hispanic/Latino (2020 Census).

For context, ZCTA 80602 as a whole (44,783 people) runs a median household income of $151,737 and a median home value of $667,000 — so Todd Creek CDP sits well above even its own affluent ZIP.

This is the buyer for a $10-12/sq ft installation, for a multi-hole putting complex rather than a single green, and for premium infill and pet systems. Sell craftsmanship, permanence and warranty here; do not lead with price.
facts.golf:
The strongest golf story of the five, and it is genuinely two-sided.

- TODD CREEK GOLF CLUB (formerly Heritage Todd Creek Golf Club) — 8455 Heritage Drive, Thornton CO 80602. 18 holes, par 72, 7,435 yards, designed by ARTHUR HILLS. Confirmed by Overpass as a golf course inside 4 km of the Todd Creek centroid. It is the golf heart of the Heritage Todd Creek 55+ community (1,300 homes, Lennar, 2006-2023), which has a 33,000 sq ft clubhouse with the Creekside Restaurant, indoor lap pool, resort outdoor pool, tennis, fitness centre and ballroom. Worth knowing for sales: 55places reports residents pay the same daily rates as non-residents — no membership benefit is bundled — which is exactly the friction that makes a backyard practice green attractive.
- RIVERDALE DUNES and RIVERDALE KNOLLS — 13300 Riverdale Road, Brighton CO 80602 (geocoded: unincorporated, no CDP), also confirmed by Overpass within range. Riverdale Dunes is a PETE DYE design that the club itself describes as "a Pete Dye designed course that has received local and national acclaim," ranked as Colorado's top public course and among America's best 75 public layouts. Riverdale Knolls is the parkland companion with canals running through it. These are Adams County-owned public courses.

So a Todd Creek homeowner has an Arthur Hills championship layout at the end of the street and a nationally ranked Pete Dye public course five minutes away. That is a serious, checkable, name-droppable golf context — and it is the single best putting-green sales environment in this batch.

The legitimate plays with these bodies are (a) replacement of turf already installed, (b) athletic fields of play, which are exempt, and (c) residential referrals through the association newsletter rather than a common-area sale.

PET: acreage households with dogs are the volume residential opportunity — dog runs and kennel surfaces on 1-acre lots where mud and dust are the year-round complaint.

name: Henderson

facts.strongest_angle:
LEAD WITH: "In Henderson you pump your own water — so a lawn does not cost you a bill, it costs you your well."

This is the only place in the batch where a large share of households have NO water utility at all. The community water systems here are astonishingly small: Hazeltine Heights Water serves 261 people on 88 connections from groundwater, and Tucson Water Company serves 90 people on 36 connections from groundwater. The rest is private domestic wells, or the annexed edges on Commerce City, Brighton and Thornton supplies. A Colorado domestic well is permitted, augmentation-constrained and finite — irrigating bluegrass through a Front Range summer draws down your own aquifer and runs your own pump, and there is no rebate coming to help.

Stack that on the soil and you have the second half of the lead: VONA SANDY LOAM at 0-1% slope, which holds almost no water, on flat open bottomland that blows dust in July and turns to slop in April. So the Henderson homeowner is pumping their own water into sand — and the paddock gate, the dog run and the strip by the barn door still look terrible.

That is a completely different argument from every other town here, and it is verifiable.

WHY THIS DIFFERS FROM ITS NEIGHBOURS:
- vs TODD CREEK, four miles north: Todd Creek's metro district gives every served property NON-POTABLE irrigation water as of March 2026 and sits on montmorillonitic Renohill clay over shale at 3-9% slope. Henderson pumps from private wells and sits on sandy Vona at 0-1%. Opposite water economics, opposite soils, opposite base specs. If the client writes one page and swaps the town name, this is the pair where a knowledgeable reader will notice immediately.
- vs NORTH WASHINGTON, which shares the identical Vona sandy loam: same ground, but North Washington is warehouses with 244 dwellings and Henderson is 13,818 people on acreage.
- vs SHAW HEIGHTS and TWIN LAKES: those are quarter-acre clay lots inside the urbanised metro with municipal water and watering-day restrictions. Henderson is acreage, horses, wells and dust.

SECONDARY HOOKS, in order:
1. HORSE PROPERTY AND DUST. Paddock aprons, wash racks, barn-door approaches, gate areas, kennel runs. This is a product almost nobody in the metro markets properly, the audience is right here around the Adams County Fairgrounds, and it justifies premium pricing because it is genuinely hard to build on sand.
2. THE ANNEXATION MAZE AS PROOF OF EXPERTISE. One ZIP code, four jurisdictions. Say plainly that a house on Brighton Road answers to Adams County, a house on Havana Street answers to Commerce City, Henderson Elementary is in Brighton, and the northern fringe answers to Thornton with its Minor Development Permit and PFAS-free documentation. Then offer to identify which one applies to the reader's address. No competitor will do this.
3. HIGH INCOME, PRACTICAL BUYER. $117,373 median household income, 3.3% poverty, 79.8% ownership, median age 34.9, 6.8% veterans, and comparatively modest degree attainment. Write technically, not aspirationally: base depth, compaction lifts, infill weight, drainage fall, warranty. This audience buys specification.
4. NO REBATE, AND SAY SO. There is no municipal turf rebate in unincorporated Henderson, the state programme closed to applications in March 2025 with funding exhausted, and homeowners were never directly eligible anyway. Honesty here is a differentiator.
5. GOLF, FRAMED FOR ACREAGE. Pete Dye's Riverdale Dunes — regularly named Colorado's best public course — is minutes away at 13300 Riverdale Road. On an acre lot you can build a real short-game area, not a token green.
6. THE FAIRGROUNDS ANCHOR. Riverdale Regional Park at 9755 Henderson Road is mid-way through a capital programme running to the 2026 Adams County Fair, including a new covered outdoor arena and new agricultural barns. It is the community's centre of gravity, it is a live county procurement pipeline, and it puts the whole equestrian audience in one place once a year.

CANNIBALISATION WARNING: Henderson (80640) and Todd Creek (80602) sit on the Brighton/Weld edge and are the two places in this batch most likely to collide with the owner's NoCo Turf Co. pages. Keep Timeless Grass & Greens' Henderson page anchored to Adams County, the Riverdale corridor and the Denver-metro framing, and check that NoCo Turf Co. is not already targeting "artificial turf Brighton CO" with the same content.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa:
THREE JURISDICTIONS, THREE RULEBOOKS — and knowing which one applies to a given address is the whole credibility play on this page.

A) UNINCORPORATED ADAMS COUNTY (Brighton Road, Riverdale Road, the Platte bottom, and the acreage generally). No city landscape permit. HONEST LIMITATION: I could not verify whether the Adams County Development Standards and Regulations contain any artificial-turf provision — the county code is hosted on adamscounty.municipalcodeonline.com, a JavaScript-only platform whose search endpoints I could not query, and the county's own site search is client-side. Confirm with Adams County Community & Economic Development on 720.523.6800 / cedd-plan@adamscountyco.gov before the page claims there are no county rules.

B) COMMERCE CITY-ANNEXED PORTIONS (Havana St, Belle Creek, Thimmig Elementary area). Commerce City municipal code and landscape standards apply — I did not verify Commerce City's specific artificial-turf provisions and the client should check them before quoting work in Belle Creek or the Havana Street subdivisions.

C) BRIGHTON-ANNEXED PORTIONS (Henderson Elementary area, 124th Avenue). City of Brighton code applies — again, unverified here.

And for the northern fringe under Thornton, the full Thornton artificial-turf regime applies: Minor Development Permit required before installation, artificial turf capped at 25% of the landscape area in front and unenclosed side yards but unlimited in rear and enclosed side yards, 3 ft buffers from property lines, 8 ft from the front building wall, tree-equivalent living plant requirements, cut-pile infill turf with backing draining at 2 inches per hour, minimum 8-year fade warranty, glued seams, a minimum 3-inch compacted aggregate sub-base, and strict PFAS-free documentation that explicitly rejects manufacturer self-testing.

STATE LAW:
- C.R.S. 38-33.3-106.5(1)(i): an association may not prohibit "the use of xeriscape, nonvegetative turf grass, or drought-tolerant vegetative landscapes," and guidelines must "not prohibit the use of nonvegetative turf grass in the backyard of a unit owner's property." Relevant to the Belle Creek, King Ranch Estates and Brantner Village HOAs.
- SB24-005, effective for local governments 2026-01-01: no new artificial turf on commercial, institutional or industrial property, on common interest community property, or in rights-of-way, parking lots, medians and transportation corridors — EXCEPT on athletic fields of play. So do not pitch decorative turf to Belle Creek's HOA common areas; do pitch the Prairie View athletic complex and the county's sports facilities under the fields-of-play exemption.

One more practical rule to know for acreage work: horse and livestock properties fall under Adams County agricultural zoning, and arena, paddock and barn surfacing may touch different standards than residential landscaping. Worth asking the county about explicitly.
facts.water_and_rules:
THE DEFINING FACT: THERE IS NO SINGLE WATER UTILITY IN HENDERSON, AND FOR MANY HOUSEHOLDS THERE IS NO UTILITY AT ALL. This is the most commercially useful water story in the batch and it is the exact opposite of Todd Creek's.

From the EPA SDWIS active community water system list for Colorado, the systems with Henderson-area service are strikingly small and groundwater-based:
- HAZELTINE HEIGHTS WATER (PWSID CO0101070), city listed as HENDERSON — 261 people, just 88 service connections, primary source GW = GROUNDWATER.
- TUCSON WATER COMPANY (PWSID CO0101158), city listed as HENDERSON — 90 people, 36 connections, GROUNDWATER.
And in the immediate Brighton-area fringe, a cluster of similar micro-systems: Hi Land Acres WSD (350 people, 115 connections, GW), Mountain View WUA (320 people, 125 connections, GW), Third Creek WUA (90 people, 39 connections, GW), North Washington WUA (90 people, 36 connections, GW), Hope Ditch Co (63 people, 23 connections, GW).

The annexed portions are served by the big utilities:
- SOUTH ADAMS COUNTY WATER AND SANITATION DISTRICT (PWSID CO0101140), Commerce City — 75,559 people, 24,754 connections, purchased surface water. (I could not fetch sacwsd.org; it blocks automated access. Restrictions and any rebate must be confirmed by phone.)
- CITY OF BRIGHTON (PWSID CO0101025) — 56,304 people, 13,031 connections, purchased surface water.
- CITY OF THORNTON (PWSID CO0101150) for the northern fringe — currently under STAGE 1 DROUGHT RESTRICTIONS effective March 15, 2026: two watering days per week of the customer's choosing, no lawn watering between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m., new sod or seed only under a 21-day permit available in May, June, September and October, and fines from $100 residential / $250 commercial / $1,000 construction after a 10-day cure period.

AND BEYOND ALL OF THAT: a substantial share of unincorporated Henderson households are on INDIVIDUAL DOMESTIC WELLS. That is the real story. A Colorado domestic well is not free water — it is a permitted, augmentation-constrained, physically finite supply, and irrigating a bluegrass lawn through a Front Range summer draws down the household's own aquifer and runs its own pump. There is no utility bill to point at, which is why the standard "save on your water bill" pitch misses; the correct pitch is "stop pumping your own water into a lawn."

TURF REBATE: none. There is no municipal rebate available to unincorporated Henderson at all — no city, no district programme found. The Colorado Water Conservation Board's Turf Replacement Grant Program stopped accepting applications in March 2025 with funding expected exhausted, and single-family homeowners were never eligible to apply directly regardless. The nearest artificial-turf rebate in the region is Thornton's ($2/sq ft, 200-1,000 sq ft, $2,000 lifetime cap per lot) and it does not reach Henderson. Be straight about this on the page.

Also live at check date: unincorporated Adams County is under Stage 1 Fire Restrictions by order of Sheriff Gene Claps.
facts.soil_and_yard:
Verified from USDA SSURGO via Soil Data Access (point query at 39.9205, -104.8658):

Map unit VoA — VONA SANDY LOAM, 0 TO 1 PERCENT SLOPES.
- Vona, 90%, well drained, "Coarse-loamy, mixed, mesic Ustollic Haplargids"
- Dacono, 5%
- Truckton, 5%

Identical to North Washington, and the polar opposite of Todd Creek four miles north. This is South Platte terrace ground: SANDY, COARSE-LOAMY, WELL DRAINED, DEAD FLAT at 0-1%. EXPANSIVE CLAY IS NOT THE LOCAL PROBLEM IN HENDERSON — and being able to say that, and to say why Todd Creek up the road is completely different, is exactly the kind of specificity that separates a real local page from a template.

What the sand actually means, in the homeowner's language:
- Water disappears. Sandy loam has low water-holding capacity, so a lawn here needs MORE irrigation than the same lawn on clay to look the same — which is brutal when you are pumping it from your own well.
- Dust and mud. Bare or thin sandy ground in a horse paddock, a dog run or a high-traffic gate area turns to dust in July and slop in April. On acreage with animals this is the number one daily complaint, and it is the emotional lead for this page.
- Wind. Flat, open, sandy South Platte bottomland with little tree cover means blowing dust and blowing infill. Specify heavier infill and proper edge anchoring, and say why.

Technically:
- Drainage is easy; the subgrade accepts water.
- COMPACTION AND SETTLEMENT are the whole risk. Loose sand consolidates under load, so proof-rolling and compaction in lifts is the difference between a flat green in year five and a dished one.
- Positive fall must be designed into the base because 0-1% ground gives you none.
- Floodplain: the South Platte and Brantner Gulch run through this area (Adams County is currently doing Brantner Gulch restoration for flood mitigation at Riverdale Regional Park). Check floodplain mapping on riverside parcels.
- LOCAL MATERIAL ADVANTAGE, worth one line on the page: this stretch of the South Platte is Denver's sand-and-gravel belt, so aggregate base material is quarried a few miles away. Shorter haul, and a supply-chain point most competitors would never think to make.

facts.housing_stock:
CHECK DATE 2026-09-07. IMPORTANT METHODOLOGICAL NOTE FIRST: Henderson is NOT a census-designated place — I confirmed it is absent from the Census Bureau's 2020 Colorado place code file, and geocoding 12000 Brighton Rd, 11500 Brighton Rd, 13300 Riverdale Rd and 9755 Henderson Rd all return "unincorporated, no CDP." There is therefore NO Census data for Henderson as such. Everything below is for ZCTA 80640, which is the correct and honest proxy, and I have said so.

ZCTA 80640 (ACS 2020-2024, Census Reporter): 13,818 people across 13 square miles, density 1,062 per sq mi.

HOUSING:
- Owner-occupied 3,821 vs renter-occupied 969 = 79.8% ownership.
- Units in structure: 3,612 single-family detached; 435 single-family attached; and 333 MOBILE HOMES — a notable share, and the highest absolute mobile-home count in this batch.
- Year built: the dominant cohort is 2000-2009 with 2,814 units, followed by 2010-2019 with 906. So despite the rural, farm-era identity, most housing in this ZIP is 21st-century production building.
- Median home value $497,100 — modest for the metro and the lowest of the three affluent-adjacent places here.
- Median age 34.9 — young.
- Average household size 2.9 persons.

WHAT THE ZIP ACTUALLY CONTAINS, AND WHY IT IS SPLIT. Henderson has been carved up by annexation. I geocoded a spread of Henderson addresses: 10001 Havana St and 10426 Havana St return COMMERCE CITY; Henderson Elementary at 12301 E 124th Ave returns BRIGHTON CITY; John W Thimmig Elementary (11453 Oswego St) and Belle Creek Charter (9290 E 107th Ave) return COMMERCE CITY; while 11500 Brighton Rd, 12000 Brighton Rd, 12100 Riverdale Rd, 13300 Riverdale Rd and 9755 Henderson Rd remain UNINCORPORATED. Wikipedia confirms portions have been annexed by Commerce City, Brighton and Thornton.

So the housing stock is really three things stacked in one ZIP:
1. UNINCORPORATED ACREAGE AND HORSE PROPERTY along Brighton Road, Riverdale Road and the South Platte bottom — older farmsteads, ranchettes, outbuildings, arenas, paddocks, plus scattered mobile homes.
2. 2000s PRODUCTION SUBDIVISIONS annexed into Commerce City and Brighton — Belle Creek (a new-urbanist neighbourhood with its own charter school and family centre), King Ranch Estates, Brantner Village and similar, on conventional 5,000-9,000 sq ft lots with HOAs.
3. MOBILE HOME COMMUNITIES — 333 units.

LOT SIZES ARE NOT VERIFIED FROM PARCEL DATA. The acreage character is inferred from the unincorporated geocoding, the horse-property landmarks and the ZIP-wide density of 1,062 per sq mi; treat specific lot figures as estimates.

HOA PREVALENCE: sharply split. Zero on the unincorporated acreage; standard suburban HOAs in the annexed 2000s subdivisions.

COMMERCIAL READ: this is a high-income, low-poverty, young-family, land-owning, practically minded market that is NOT university-credentialled and NOT design-magazine driven. They will pay well for something built right and demonstrably durable, and they will be unusually receptive to a technical explanation of base construction, drainage and infill. They will be turned off by luxury-lifestyle copy. Aim for the upper half of the price range on craftsmanship and warranty, not on aesthetics.

name: Shaw Heights

facts.strongest_angle:
LEAD WITH: "The most crowded back yards in the north metro — on a slope, over clay that moves."

Shaw Heights has 8,226 people per square mile achieved with ZERO apartment buildings — 1,674 detached houses and 3.3 people per household on lots of roughly 7,000-8,000 square feet, on 3 to 5 percent slopes over smectitic Platner clay. No other town in this batch has that combination. The lead should be about a yard that is genuinely worn out: kids, dogs, extended family, everyone outside, on grass that runs downhill and never recovers.

That is a DURABILITY page, not a water page and not a luxury page.

WHY THIS DIFFERS FROM ITS NEIGHBOURS:
- vs TWIN LAKES, four miles south-east and on the same soil series: Twin Lakes is bimodal (40% built in the 1950s, 36% after 2010) and includes a new-build metro-district community; Shaw Heights has built NOTHING since about 2005 and has no apartments at all. Twin Lakes is 0-3% flat; Shaw Heights is 3-5% and needs cycle-and-soak just to wet the soil. Twin Lakes households average 2.4 people; Shaw Heights 3.3. Same clay, completely different job.
- vs TODD CREEK: acreage, $194K income, montmorillonitic shale on up to 9%, golf-community identity. Shaw Heights is $86K income, a quarter-acre lot and a public golf course down the road.
- vs WESTMINSTER, which surrounds it on all sides: this is the point of leverage. Shaw Heights is NOT Westminster. No city landscape code, no permit — and a homeowner three streets away inside city limits is playing by different rules.

SECONDARY HOOKS, in order:
1. THE ENCLAVE IDENTITY. "Surrounded by Westminster, governed by Adams County." Locals know they are an island and rather like it. Owning that distinction — and knowing which side of the line a given address falls on — is instant credibility, and I have confirmed the geocoding method to check any address.
2. RUNOFF IS THE VISIBLE SYMPTOM. Westminster's own guidance tells people to split watering into three short cycles to stop runoff. Open the technical section with the sheet of water going down the driveway. Then explain that a turf base built with geotextile separation, compacted aggregate and downhill edge restraint solves the runoff, the burnt bottom of the yard and the muddy patch by the gate all at once.
3. NO REBATE, SO NO WAITING. Westminster's incentives buy plants, not turf; there is no artificial-turf rebate here, unlike Thornton's $2/sq ft. Say so honestly and pivot to bill savings, no reseeding, no mowing and no water-restriction anxiety.
4. HOUSEHOLD SIZE AS THE PROOF POINT. 3.3 people per household and a 9.5% annual birth rate among women 15-50 — write for young families and grandparents in the same house. Pet turf and play areas, not showpiece landscaping.
5. LANGUAGE. 39.5% Hispanic or Latino and 13.1% foreign-born. A Spanish-language version of this page, or at minimum a Spanish-speaking estimator called out on it, will out-convert any design improvement.

PRICE POSITIONING: this is the volume page. Median home value $482,800 — the lowest in the batch. Do not force the $10-12/sq ft ambition here; win the neighbourhood on referrals and let Todd Creek carry the premium.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa:
NO CITY PERMIT, NO HOA — the cleanest regulatory environment in the batch, and worth saying so directly.

- Shaw Heights is unincorporated Adams County, not Westminster. Even though it is completely surrounded by Westminster, city landscape codes do not govern these lots. Compare Thornton across the metro, where artificial turf needs a Minor Development Permit, is capped at 25% of a front-yard landscape area, and comes with mandatory buffers, tree-equivalent planting and PFAS documentation. None of that binds Shaw Heights.
- HOA coverage is low: this is 1960s-70s unincorporated tract housing that largely predates the covenant era. Northridge Manor, Hillcrest and Abbey are neighbourhood names rather than governed associations. Where a covenant does exist, C.R.S. 38-33.3-106.5(1)(i) still applies — an association may not prohibit "the use of xeriscape, nonvegetative turf grass, or drought-tolerant vegetative landscapes," and guidelines must "not prohibit the use of nonvegetative turf grass in the backyard of a unit owner's property."

HONEST LIMITATION, same as the other unincorporated pages: I could not verify whether the Adams County Development Standards and Regulations contain an artificial-turf provision. The county code lives on adamscounty.municipalcodeonline.com, a JavaScript-only platform whose search I could not query. Confirm with Adams County Community & Economic Development, 720.523.6800 / cedd-plan@adamscountyco.gov before asserting there are no county rules.

SB24-005 (effective for local governments 2026-01-01) prohibits new artificial turf on commercial, institutional, industrial and common interest community property and in rights-of-way, medians and parking lots, with an explicit exemption for athletic fields of play. Private residential yards are unaffected. Practical effect here: residential is wide open; school and district common-area work needs to be framed as athletic fields or as replacement of existing turf.
facts.water_and_rules:
HONEST GAP TO CLOSE BEFORE PUBLISHING: I could NOT definitively confirm which utility serves Shaw Heights. Here is what I established and what remains open.

- Shaw Heights is an unincorporated island roughly between 84th and 88th Avenues, Federal Boulevard to Sheridan Boulevard, ZIP 80031/80030, entirely surrounded by the City of Westminster. Confirmed by geocoding 8780 Circle Dr, 9100 Lowell Blvd and 8731 Lowell Blvd, all of which return Shaw Heights CDP, while 8641 Lowell Blvd and 8500 Sheridan Blvd return Westminster city — so the enclave is small and irregular.
- The EPA SDWIS active community water system list for Colorado contains NO system named for Shaw Heights. The plausible suppliers are CITY OF WESTMINSTER (PWSID CO0101170, 202,078 people, 33,619 connections, own surface supply) serving the enclave by agreement, or CRESTVIEW WATER AND SANITATION DISTRICT (PWSID CO0101040) whose stated boundary runs "Tennyson Street on the west to I-25 on the east then 56th avenue on the south to Sherrylwood Lane on the north" — Shaw Heights sits north and partly west of that, so Crestview looks UNLIKELY. There is also CASA ESTATES MHP (PWSID CO0101167, Westminster, 1,117 people, 366 connections, purchased surface water), a small park system in the vicinity.
- ACTION: the client should confirm by address with the City of Westminster Utilities before the page states a provider. Do not guess in print.

IF WESTMINSTER SERVES IT, these are the rules I verified on westminsterco.gov (2026-09-07): Westminster advises watering TWICE WEEKLY under normal conditions with an optional third day in extreme heat, and pushes the "cycle and soak" method — "Divide watering times into three short cycles to reduce runoff and grow a strong, healthy lawn." (Note how directly that speaks to the 3-5% slope here.) The city references a 2026 Irrigation Season and a dedicated drought webpage for current status; I could not extract a declared drought stage.

REBATES AND ARTIFICIAL TURF: Westminster's incentives are a free-toilet programme for income-qualified homeowners, free indoor water-use inspections, and three Resource Central programmes — Garden In A Box, Slow the Flow sprinkler evaluations, and the Lawn Replacement Program. All of the landscape money is for replacing grass with WATER-WISE PLANTS. Westminster's own "Turf Conversion" page is about converting CITY PARK turf (City Hall and Faversham Park) to native grass, not a residential rebate. I found NO artificial-turf rebate available in Westminster. Contrast this explicitly with Thornton, which pays $2/sq ft for artificial turf — a Shaw Heights homeowner gets nothing, so the page must sell on bill savings and durability, not on an incentive.

STATE PROGRAMME: the CWCB Turf Replacement Grant Program stopped taking applications in March 2025 and expects funding exhausted; homeowners and HOAs were never directly eligible.

Also live at check date: unincorporated Adams County is under Stage 1 Fire Restrictions by order of Sheriff Gene Claps.
facts.soil_and_yard:
Verified from USDA SSURGO via Soil Data Access (point query at 39.8553, -105.0414):

Map unit PlC — PLATNER LOAM, 3 TO 5 PERCENT SLOPES.
- Platner, 85%, well drained, "Fine, SMECTITIC, mesic Aridic Paleustolls"
- Wages, 10%, well drained, fine-loamy
- Stoneham, 5%, well drained, fine-loamy Haplustalfs

This is the SAME expansive smectitic clay series as Twin Lakes — but on 3 TO 5 PERCENT SLOPES rather than 0 to 3. That single difference is the entire technical story of this page and it is exactly the kind of specific, checkable distinction the client asked for.

WHY THE SLOPE MATTERS ON CLAY, in terms a homeowner recognises:
- Water runs off before it soaks in. Every Shaw Heights homeowner has watched their sprinklers push a sheet of water down the driveway and into the gutter. That is why Westminster teaches "cycle and soak" — three short cycles instead of one long one. It is also why half these lawns are green at the top of the yard and burnt at the bottom.
- Under Crestview/Denver Water-style and Westminster-style rules alike, runoff onto streets and gutters is a violation, not just waste.
- For a turf install, a 3-5% fall means the base must be built to hold position: geotextile separation over the clay subgrade, properly compacted aggregate, and edge restraint at the downhill side or the base creeps. Seams run across the slope, not with it.
- Smectitic subsoil means shrink-swell. On a slope that translates into differential movement — one part of a yard heaving while another shrinks — which is precisely what makes a cheap install go wavy in year three. This is the argument for paying for a proper base.

So the technical hook for Shaw Heights is: SLOPE PLUS CLAY PLUS HEAVY USE. Not "expansive soils" as boilerplate, but "your yard runs downhill, the clay under it moves, and three-and-a-bit people per household are walking on it every day."

Elevation 5,512 ft — the highest of the five places. CDP area 0.701 sq mi.
facts.housing_stock:
CHECK DATE 2026-09-07. The most uniform housing stock in the batch, and unusually dense for detached housing.

ACS 2020-2024 (Census Reporter, geoid 16000US0869480), 1,783 housing units, year structure built:
- 1950-59: 299
- 1960-69: 781  (44% — the defining cohort)
- 1970-79: 553  (31%)
- 1980-89: 56
- 1990-99: 82
- 2000-09: 12
- 2010-19: 0
- 2020 or later: 0

NOTHING has been built here since roughly 2005. Ninety-two percent of the stock predates 1980. This is a finished, static, 1960s-70s tract enclave — the north-metro equivalent of a time capsule.

Units in structure (B25024): 1,674 single-family detached; 100 single-family attached; 9 mobile homes; and ZERO units in any multifamily building of any size. No duplexes, no fourplexes, no apartments at all. That is remarkable given the density.

DENSITY: population density 8,226 per square mile over just 0.701 sq mi — the highest in this batch by a mile — achieved entirely with detached houses. Derived lot size: 0.701 sq mi = 449 acres against 1,783 units = roughly 10,900 sq ft gross per unit including all streets and public land, which nets out to something like a 7,000-8,000 sq ft lot. That is a real back yard, not a courtyard. LOT SIZES ARE DERIVED, NOT PULLED FROM PARCEL DATA — flag as approximate.

Tenure (B25003): 1,386 owner-occupied vs 302 renter-occupied = 82.1% ownership. Median gross rent $2,125 — high, because the rental stock is whole detached houses, not apartments.

Median home value $482,800 — the lowest of the four CDPs measured here and about $105,000 below Twin Lakes. This is the affordable-detached corner of the north metro.

HOA PREVALENCE: low. 1960s-70s unincorporated Adams County tract subdivisions of this vintage largely predate the covenant era. Named neighbourhoods inside or adjacent per OpenStreetMap: Northridge Manor, Hillcrest, Abbey. The absence of an ARC process is a selling point.

Typical product: single-storey brick-and-siding ranches, split-levels and tri-levels of the Westminster/Arvada 1960s-70s idiom, attached single or double garages, mature Siberian elms and ash, and original bluegrass front and back on a lot that slopes.
facts.who_lives_there:
Population 5,565 (ACS 2020-2024); 5,185 at the 2020 Census, up only 1.3% from 2010's 5,116 — essentially flat for fifteen years, consistent with zero new construction.

- Median household income $86,250.
- Per capita income $34,420 — the low per-capita against a decent household income is the tell: lots of people per household, several earners.
- AVERAGE HOUSEHOLD SIZE 3.3 PERSONS across 1,688 households — the largest in this batch and well above Colorado norms. Multigenerational and extended-family households are the norm here.
- Median age 33.9 — the youngest of the five.
- Poverty 12.3% (682 residents).
- Foreign-born 13.1%.
- Education: 80.4% high school or higher, 25.9% bachelor's or higher — the lowest attainment in the batch.
- 9.5% of women aged 15-50 gave birth in the past year — a high fertility rate, lots of small children.
- Mean commute 28.7 minutes. 12.3% moved in the past year. Veterans 3.6%.

name: North Washington

facts.strongest_angle:
LEAD WITH: "North Washington is where Denver's grass stops and the freight yards start — so this page is about buildings, not back yards."

This is the one town in the batch that should NOT be written as a residential page, and the honest framing is the differentiator. 244 housing units in five and a half square miles, 64 of them mobile homes, nothing built since 2009, median age 58.4, poverty 24.4%, average household 1.4 people, and the Census Bureau will not even publish a median household income because the sample is too small. Writing a cheerful "transform your North Washington back yard" page would be a lie that locals and Google would both see through.

Write it instead as the COMMERCIAL AND INDUSTRIAL page for the I-25 / South Platte corridor, and make the lead the thing nobody else will say out loud: SINCE 1 JANUARY 2026, COLORADO SB24-005 HAS PROHIBITED NEW ARTIFICIAL TURF ON COMMERCIAL, INSTITUTIONAL AND INDUSTRIAL PROPERTY, ON HOA COMMON AREAS AND IN RIGHTS-OF-WAY, MEDIANS AND PARKING LOTS — WITH ONE EXEMPTION: ATHLETIC FIELDS OF PLAY. A page that explains that clearly, tells a property manager exactly what they can and cannot install, and then offers the two legal routes (fields of play, and replacement of turf already in place) will out-rank and out-convert every competitor still selling decorative office-park lawn that is now illegal to install.

The second lead is the indoor market. This corridor is Denver's industrial-conversion belt: climbing gyms, CrossFit boxes, sports-performance facilities, dog daycares and golf-simulator venues taking cheap warehouse space between the Post plant, the rail yards and RiNo. Indoor turf is outside the landscaping prohibition entirely and is exactly the product the owner already sells (indoor sports facilities, sports fields, pet turf).

WHY THIS DIFFERS FROM ITS NEIGHBOURS:
- vs TWIN LAKES, which it directly borders: Twin Lakes has 3,455 housing units, North Washington has 244. Twin Lakes is smectitic Platner clay; North Washington is Vona SANDY loam at 0-1% slope with no expansive-clay problem at all. Two adjoining CDPs, opposite soils and opposite markets.
- vs HENDERSON, which shares the same Vona sandy loam: Henderson is residential acreage on private wells; North Washington is warehouses and rail on the same sand. Same ground, different building.
- vs SHAW HEIGHTS / TODD CREEK: both are residential-first pages with clay and slope stories. This one has neither.

SECONDARY HOOKS:
1. THE SOIL IS THE GOOD NEWS. Say plainly that on this side of the metro the ground is sandy and flat, it drains, and the enemy is settlement rather than heave — so the base spec is about compaction in lifts and built-in fall, not about drainage escape routes. It is a small, technical, verifiably true point that reads as real local knowledge.
2. THE DENVER POST ADDRESS. 5990 Washington Street is the one address in this CDP a Denver reader recognises instantly — use it to establish place, and verify its current operating status first.
3. RIVERSIDE CEMETERY AS THE PARABLE. Colorado's oldest operating cemetery, just over the line in Denver, went brown when its water went away. It is the most vivid irrigation-economics story on the Front Range. Cite it as nearby context, never as "in North Washington."
4. FLOODPLAIN AND FREIGHT. Base builds near the Platte need floodplain checking; work near the rail yards and truck courts needs staging discipline. Naming those constraints is how you sound like the contractor who has actually worked the corridor.

IF THE CLIENT ONLY HAS BUDGET FOR FOUR TOWN PAGES IN THIS BATCH, THIS IS THE ONE TO CUT AS A TOWN PAGE AND FOLD INTO A CORRIDOR-WIDE COMMERCIAL / SB24-005 SERVICE PAGE INSTEAD. That would rank better and mislead nobody.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa:
THE DEFINING REGULATORY FACT FOR THIS PAGE IS SB24-005, AND IT CUTS AGAINST A NAIVE COMMERCIAL PITCH. Get this right and the page becomes a genuine authority piece; get it wrong and the client sells work that cannot legally be installed.

COLORADO SB24-005 (signed 2024-03-15; local-government effective date 2026-01-01, i.e. ALREADY IN FORCE at this check date) prohibits the installation of NONFUNCTIONAL TURF, ARTIFICIAL TURF and invasive plant species on:
- commercial, institutional or industrial property
- common interest community property
- street rights-of-way, parking lots, medians and transportation corridors
with an EXPLICIT EXEMPTION for artificial turf "on athletic fields of play." State facilities were covered from 2025-01-01 for projects whose design began on or after that date.

North Washington CDP is, by land area, almost entirely commercial and industrial. So the honest commercial offer here is narrow and specific:
1. ATHLETIC FIELDS OF PLAY — exempt, and this is the real opportunity: indoor training facilities, sports-performance gyms, warehouse-conversion field houses, batting and golf bays. The industrial building stock in this corridor is exactly what indoor sports operators convert.
2. REPLACEMENT of artificial turf ALREADY INSTALLED before the prohibition.
3. PET AND ANIMAL FACILITIES — dog daycares, boarding kennels, veterinary runs. These need careful legal review against the prohibition; the client should get written guidance rather than assume.
4. INDOOR installations generally, which the landscaping prohibition does not reach.

What the page should NOT sell: decorative artificial lawn on a new office forecourt, a warehouse frontage, a median or a parking-lot island. That is now prohibited, and saying so out loud is the single most authoritative thing this page can do.

RESIDENTIAL: private single-family yards are not covered by SB24-005. For the 244 dwellings here, there is no city permit (unincorporated Adams County) and effectively no HOA. C.R.S. 38-33.3-106.5(1)(i) applies where covenants exist — an association may not prohibit "the use of xeriscape, nonvegetative turf grass, or drought-tolerant vegetative landscapes," and guidelines must "not prohibit the use of nonvegetative turf grass in the backyard of a unit owner's property."

HONEST LIMITATION: I could not verify whether the Adams County Development Standards and Regulations contain an artificial-turf provision — the code is on adamscounty.municipalcodeonline.com, a JavaScript-only platform I could not search. Confirm with Adams County Community & Economic Development, 720.523.6800 / cedd-plan@adamscountyco.gov.
facts.water_and_rules:
WATER PROVIDER: NORTH WASHINGTON STREET WATER AND SANITATION DISTRICT, EPA SDWIS PWSID CO0101105, population served 14,500, 3,637 service connections, primary source code SWP = PURCHASED SURFACE WATER. Note the mismatch worth understanding: the district serves 14,500 people while the CDP itself holds only a few hundred residents — the district's service area extends well beyond the CDP into Welby and the surrounding unincorporated area, and a large share of its connections are commercial and industrial.

There is also a tiny NORTH WASHINGTON WATER USERS ASSOCIATION (PWSID CO0101110, 90 people, 36 connections, groundwater) with a Brighton address — a separate small system.

HONEST GAP: I could not locate a working public website for North Washington Street Water and Sanitation District (I tried several likely domains, all dead), so I could NOT verify its specific watering restrictions or any rebate programme. Because it buys treated surface water in the Denver Water service region, the Denver Water annual rules are the likely operating regime — for reference, the neighbouring Crestview district, also on purchased surface water, publishes: in effect May 1 to October 1, "Water two days per week, adding a third day only when needed. (Watering more than three days is not allowed.)" and "lawn watering is NOT allowed between 10 am and 6 pm," plus no runoff onto streets and gutters and a 10-day deadline to fix leaks. DO NOT PUBLISH THOSE AS NORTH WASHINGTON'S RULES WITHOUT CALLING THE DISTRICT. The client should confirm directly.

TURF REBATE: none found for this district. Denver Water's landscape money (ColoradoScape / turfgrass removal through Resource Central) buys water-wise PLANTS, and its 2026 discounts of up to $750 are already "all been allocated to customer projects for the year." The Colorado Water Conservation Board's Turf Replacement Grant Program stopped accepting applications in March 2025 with funding expected exhausted, and commercial, industrial and institutional entities were explicitly listed as INELIGIBLE to apply directly anyway. So: no rebate story on this page at all.

Also live at check date: unincorporated Adams County is under Stage 1 Fire Restrictions by order of Sheriff Gene Claps.
facts.soil_and_yard:
Verified from USDA SSURGO via Soil Data Access (point query at 39.8072, -104.9789):

Map unit VoA — VONA SANDY LOAM, 0 TO 1 PERCENT SLOPES.
- Vona, 90%, well drained, taxonomic class "Coarse-loamy, mixed, mesic Ustollic Haplargids"
- Dacono, 5%
- Truckton, 5%

THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE WESTERN CDPs AND IT IS A GENUINE SELLING POINT. Vona is a COARSE-LOAMY, SANDY, well-drained soil on essentially dead-flat ground (0-1%). There is no smectitic or montmorillonitic clay here. EXPANSIVE CLAY IS NOT THE LOCAL PROBLEM IN NORTH WASHINGTON — which means the page can say something no competitor's template says: on this side of the metro the ground drains, and the risk is settlement, not heave.

What that changes technically:
- Drainage design is easy. A sandy subgrade takes water, so the base does not need the aggressive perimeter drainage a Todd Creek or Shaw Heights install requires.
- COMPACTION IS THE WHOLE JOB. Loose sandy loam under a slab of turf will consolidate and dish if it is not properly proof-rolled and compacted in lifts. The failure mode here is a sunken low spot and a rippled seam, not a heaved wave.
- Flat ground at 0-1% means positive fall has to be BUILT INTO the base, because the site gives you none. On a commercial forecourt or a truck-yard median that matters.
- Elevation 5,191 ft. The CDP holds 161 acres of water — the South Platte, Clear Creek's confluence and the gravel-pit ponds (Copeland Lake and Heron Pond sit on or just over the boundary).
- Being in the river bottom, parts of the CDP are floodplain. Any commercial base build near the Platte should be checked against Adams County floodplain mapping.
facts.housing_stock:
CHECK DATE 2026-09-07. BE HONEST ON THIS PAGE: the residential market here is genuinely tiny. If the client wants a North Washington page it should be a COMMERCIAL page with a small residential footnote, and I would rather say that than pad it.

ACS 2020-2024 (Census Reporter, geoid 16000US0854750), just 244 housing units in total across 5.426 sq mi. Year structure built:
- 1939 or earlier: 50  (20%)
- 1950-59: 109  (45%)
- 1960-69: 39
- 1970-79: 36
- 1980-89: 0
- 1990-99: 0
- 2000-09: 10
- 2010-19: 0
- 2020 or later: 0

Nothing has been built since 2009, and only ten units this century. Seventy percent of the stock is pre-1960 and a fifth of it predates 1939 — pre-war workers' cottages and farm-era houses along the South Platte and the rail corridor.

Units in structure (B25024): 180 single-family detached, 64 MOBILE HOMES (26% of all housing), and ZERO units of anything else — no attached, no duplex, no apartments.

Tenure (B25003): 104 owner-occupied vs 61 renter-occupied across 165 households — 63% ownership, the lowest in the batch.

Median home value $572,000, which sounds high against the poverty and age profile and almost certainly reflects land value in an industrial corridor rather than house quality.

DENSITY: 3,473 acres of which 161 acres is water, holding 244 dwellings. That is 14 acres per dwelling. The CDP is overwhelmingly NOT residential — it is warehouses, freight yards, the Denver Post plant, gravel operations and the South Platte bottom.

HOA PREVALENCE: effectively nil.
facts.who_lives_there:
A very small, old, poor, and partly immigrant residual population inside an industrial district.

ACS 2020-2024: population 294 (the 2020 Census counted 733, up 51.4% from 484 in 2010 — the ACS and decennial figures diverge sharply here because the universe is so small; treat both as soft).

- MEDIAN AGE 58.4 — twenty years older than metro Denver's 37.3 and the oldest in this batch by a distance.
- Per capita income $37,540, about two thirds of the state and metro figures. Median household income NOT AVAILABLE — the sample is too small for the Census Bureau to publish it, which itself tells you how thin this market is.
- POVERTY RATE 24.4% — more than double Colorado's 9.4% and metro Denver's 8.4%.
- AVERAGE HOUSEHOLD SIZE 1.4 PERSONS — very small households, many single older people.
- 22.8% foreign-born, notably higher than state and metro rates.
- Education: 73.6% high school or higher, 27.1% bachelor's or higher.
- 17% moved in the past year, above regional and national rates — churn in the rental and mobile-home stock.
- Population density about 142 per sq mi, or 56.6 per sq mi on the ACS figure.

TRANSLATION FOR THE PAGE: 165 households, a quarter of them below the poverty line, average age approaching 60, a quarter of the housing on wheels. Do not write a residential lead here. There is no realistic volume of $10-12/sq ft back-yard work in North Washington. The money in this ZIP is in buildings, not houses.
facts.golf:
There is no golf course in or adjacent to North Washington CDP, and the page should not pretend otherwise.

Nearest named facilities, all in Denver and all a drive away:
- City Park Golf Course (Denver municipal), to the south-east.
- Willis Case Golf Course (Denver municipal, 4999 Vrain St), to the west.
- The former Park Hill Golf Club site to the east, now the subject of redevelopment.

If the client wants a golf angle in this corridor it has to be commercial and indoor: putting surfaces in office and warehouse-conversion amenity spaces, brewery and taproom patios, and golf simulator or short-game facilities in the RiNo/Globeville industrial-conversion market immediately south. That is a legitimate niche and a genuinely different pitch from a residential putting green.
facts.commercial_targets:
There are NO public schools inside North Washington CDP. That is a real finding, not a gap — it confirms the residential population is too small to support one.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY HERE, AND HOW TO SELL IT:

1. INDUSTRIAL AND LOGISTICS PROPERTY OWNERS along the Washington Street / Brighton Boulevard / I-25 corridor. The Denver Post plant at 5990 Washington Street is the anchor address. The sale is indoor amenity space, training areas and athletic-field-of-play installations, NOT exterior landscaping — SB24-005 prohibits new artificial turf on industrial property outdoors.
2. INDOOR SPORTS AND FITNESS OPERATORS converting industrial shells. Mountain Strong Denver Climbing and CrossFit sits within range and is exactly the profile. The whole Globeville / Elyria-Swansea / RiNo industrial-conversion belt immediately south is the richest indoor-turf market in the metro, and the athletic-fields-of-play exemption in SB24-005 makes it the legally clean one.
3. PET BUSINESSES. Dog daycare, boarding and veterinary operations cluster in cheap industrial space exactly like this. Worth a direct canvass of the Washington Street and Brighton Boulevard corridors — OpenStreetMap coverage of these small businesses is poor and I would rather flag that than invent a list.
4. LARADON (Laradon Hall Society for Exceptional Children and Adults), Lincoln Street — a long-established disability services campus with vocational facilities and outdoor space. Institutional property, so new decorative turf is prohibited, but accessible play and therapy surfaces framed as fields of play are a legitimate conversation.
5. NATIONAL WESTERN CENTER, 4655 Humboldt Street (in Denver, immediately south) — a multi-year, publicly funded campus redevelopment with equestrian, event and exhibition space. Large, ongoing, and the kind of project where an installer who understands SB24-005 and the athletic-field exemption has a real advantage.
6. THE MOBILE HOME COMMUNITIES — 64 of the CDP's 244 units. Park owners are a single decision-maker controlling many small yards and common areas. Small-ticket, but a genuine niche nobody else is calling.
7. Stapleton Recreation Center (Denver Parks) sits within range as a public-sector prospect.

WHAT I DID NOT FIND: named daycares, named schools, named HOA common areas inside the CDP. There aren't any. Say so.
facts.landmarks:
CONFIRMED INSIDE NORTH WASHINGTON CDP by Census Geocoder:
- THE DENVER POST — 5990 Washington Street. Wikipedia records that "In 2017, The Denver Post announced that its headquarters were moving to its printing plant in North Washington in Adams County, Colorado," and the Wikipedia article on the CDP notes the paper "is headquartered and printed in North Washington." This is by far the most recognisable address in the CDP. CAVEAT: I could not confirm the plant's CURRENT operating status from the sources available, and newspaper printing operations have been consolidating nationally — verify before writing about it in the present tense.
- 6500 Washington Street and the Washington Street industrial corridor generally.

IMMEDIATELY ADJACENT BUT NOT INSIDE THE CDP — I checked these and they geocode to DENVER CITY, so describe them as neighbouring, not local:

- Riverside Cemetery, 5201 Brighton Boulevard (Denver) — Colorado's oldest operating cemetery, famous locally for going brown after its irrigation water was sold off. It is the perfect illustration of what irrigation costs in this corridor, but it is in Denver, so cite it as context, not as a local landmark.
- Heron Pond / Heller / Carpio-Sanguinette Park and South Platte Riverfront Park (Denver's Globeville park system).
- Globeville, Elyria-Swansea and Chaffee Park — the Denver neighbourhoods that border the CDP.
- Laradon (Laradon Hall Society for Exceptional Children and Adults) and the Laradon Vocational Center, on Lincoln Street.

GEOGRAPHIC ANCHORS INSIDE OR ON THE EDGE: the South Platte River, the Clear Creek confluence, Copeland Lake, the I-25 / I-70 interchange and the Union Pacific yards, and the Twin Lakes Park open space at the CDP's north-west corner.

name: Twin Lakes

facts.strongest_angle:
LEAD WITH: "Two Twin Lakes, two completely different turf jobs — and we quote them differently."

This is the only place in the batch where 40% of the housing was built in the 1950s and 36% was built after 2010, with almost nothing in between (just 61 of 3,455 units built 1990-2009). The page should open by naming both halves explicitly — the post-war brick ranches on flat lots with 70-year-old bluegrass and no HOA, and Midtown at Clear Creek's alley-loaded courtyard yards with a metro district and a design review board — and then give each its own scope, its own base build and its own price band. That structure alone will read as local knowledge no competitor has, because most competitors do not even know Midtown is in Adams County rather than Denver.

WHY THIS DIFFERS FROM ITS NEIGHBOURS:
- vs SHAW HEIGHTS (same soil series, same county, 4 miles north-west): Shaw Heights is monolithic 1960s-70s tract housing with zero apartments, 3.3 people per household and no new construction since 2005 — one job type, one story. Twin Lakes is bimodal. Shaw Heights also sits on 3-5% slope; Twin Lakes is 0-3% flat.
- vs TODD CREEK: Todd Creek is acreage, $194K median income and non-potable irrigation water. Twin Lakes is $95K median income on small lots with Denver Water restrictions and no rebate.
- vs NORTH WASHINGTON, which it borders: North Washington is industrial with 244 housing units. Twin Lakes has 3,455.

SECONDARY HOOKS, in order:
1. NO CITY PERMIT. Unincorporated Adams County — no Minor Development Permit, no 25% front-yard cap, none of the Thornton buffer and tree-equivalent rules. Say it plainly and contrast it with Thornton by name.
2. THE REBATE IS NOT COMING. Crestview passes rebates through to Denver Water; Denver Water pays for water-wise PLANTS, not artificial turf, and its 2026 turfgrass removal discounts are already fully allocated. Being the installer who tells the truth about this builds more trust than pretending a rebate exists.
3. THE RESTRICTION IS THE REAL PAIN. May 1 to October 1, two days a week (three only when needed), nothing between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m. A 1950s bluegrass lawn cannot be kept green on that schedule on a smectitic clay subsoil. That is the emotional hook.
4. TWO DOG PARKS IN ONE SUBDIVISION. Midtown's dog density plus courtyard-sized yards is the cleanest pet-turf argument in the batch.
5. HOA ANSWER READY: quote C.R.S. 38-33.3-106.5 — a Colorado association cannot prohibit nonvegetative turf grass in a backyard — and offer a done-for-you design review submittal for Midtown owners.

TONE: this is a value-plus-value page, not a luxury page. Median home value $587,500, median income $95,583. Put the $10-12/sq ft ambition into the Midtown half and the putting-green upsell, and keep the 1950s half honest and volume-priced.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa:
NO MUNICIPAL PERMIT — this is Twin Lakes' single biggest regulatory selling point, and it is a direct contrast with the Thornton-governed parts of this metro.

Twin Lakes is unincorporated Adams County. There is no city artificial-turf permit here. Compare Thornton, a few miles east, where a MINOR DEVELOPMENT PERMIT is required before artificial turf is installed as landscaping, front/unenclosed-side turf is capped at 25% of the landscape area, and there are mandatory 3 ft property-line buffers, an 8 ft buffer from the front building wall, tree-equivalent planting requirements and PFAS-free documentation. None of that applies in unincorporated Twin Lakes.

HONEST LIMITATION: I could NOT confirm whether the Adams County Development Standards and Regulations themselves contain any artificial-turf provision. The county moved its code to adamscounty.municipalcodeonline.com, a JavaScript-only platform whose search endpoints I could not query, and the county site's own search is client-side. Before publishing "no county rules," the client should ring Adams County Community & Economic Development at 720.523.6800 / cedd-plan@adamscountyco.gov and get it in writing. Do not assert the absence of a county rule as fact on the page.

STATE LAW THAT DOES APPLY:
1. C.R.S. 38-33.3-106.5 (CCIOA). An association may not prohibit "the use of xeriscape, nonvegetative turf grass, or drought-tolerant vegetative landscapes" (subsection (1)(i)), and association guidelines must "not prohibit the use of nonvegetative turf grass in the backyard of a unit owner's property." This is the line to put in front of every Midtown at Clear Creek homeowner whose HOA pushes back: in Colorado, a backyard artificial lawn cannot be banned outright. Associations may still regulate appearance and require design review — so the page should promise a compliant submittal package, not a fight.
2. Colorado SB24-005 (signed 2024-03-15, effective for local governments 2026-01-01) prohibits installing nonfunctional turf, ARTIFICIAL TURF and invasive plant species on commercial, institutional or industrial property, common interest community property, and street rights-of-way / parking lots / medians / transportation corridors — with an explicit exemption for artificial turf "on athletic fields of play." Private residential yards are not the target. Practical effect for Twin Lakes: sell residential all day; do NOT pitch new artificial turf for Midtown's HOA/metro-district common areas.
facts.water_and_rules:
WATER PROVIDER: Crestview Water and Sanitation District (EPA SDWIS PWSID CO0101040), population served 23,756, 4,491 service connections, primary source code SWP = purchased surface water. Crestview's own site describes its boundary as "roughly, Tennyson Street on the west to I-25 on the east then 56th avenue on the south to Sherrylwood Lane on the north," which encloses the Twin Lakes CDP. Parts of the CDP fringe may fall to North Pecos Water & Sanitation District (PWSID CO0116553, 2,500 people, 402 connections, also purchased surface water) — verify by address.

WATERING RESTRICTIONS (verified on Crestview's Summer Watering Rules page, 2026-09-07): in effect MAY 1 TO OCTOBER 1. "Water two days per week, adding a third day only when needed. (Watering more than three days is not allowed.)" And "lawn watering is NOT allowed between 10 am and 6 pm." Also: no watering during rain or high wind, no runoff onto streets/gutters/hard surfaces, leaking systems must be fixed within 10 days, shut-off nozzles required for vehicle washing, mow cool-season grass to 2.5-3.5 inches. This is the Denver Water annual rule set.

REBATES — AND THE KEY DIFFERENCE FROM THORNTON: Crestview's residential rebates page states plainly that "Denver Water processes all of the water related fixture rebates for Crestview Water and Sanitation District Customers." Denver Water's landscape program is ColoradoScape / turfgrass removal, delivered through Resource Central, and it pays for replacing bluegrass with WATER-WISE PLANTS. As of the 2026-09-07 check, Denver Water's own page says: "Due to popularity, the turfgrass removal discounts for 2026 have all been allocated to customer projects for the year" (the discount was up to $750 off 2026 turfgrass removal services).

I found NO artificial-turf rebate available to Twin Lakes households. That is the opposite of Thornton next door, which does pay $2/sq ft for artificial turf. So the Twin Lakes page must NOT promise a rebate — it should say the rebate money here is plants-only and already spent for 2026, and sell on water bill + restriction relief instead.

STATE PROGRAM: the Colorado Water Conservation Board Turf Replacement Grant Program stopped accepting applications in March 2025 and expects funding exhausted; single-family homeowners and HOAs were never eligible to apply directly anyway.

Also live at check date: unincorporated Adams County is under Stage 1 Fire Restrictions by order of Sheriff Gene Claps (banner on adamscountyco.gov, 2026-09-07).
facts.soil_and_yard:
Verified from USDA SSURGO via Soil Data Access (point query at 39.8243, -105.0064):

Map unit PlB — PLATNER LOAM, 0 TO 3 PERCENT SLOPES.
- Platner, 85% of the unit, well drained, taxonomic class "Fine, SMECTITIC, mesic Aridic Paleustolls"
- Ascalon, 10%, well drained, fine-loamy
- Rago, 5%, well drained, "Fine, smectitic, mesic Pachic Argiustolls"

SMECTITIC is the operative word: smectite is the shrink-swell clay family. Platner has a dense clayey argillic (clay-accumulation) subsoil. So yes — EXPANSIVE CLAY IS A REAL, DOCUMENTED LOCAL CONDITION in Twin Lakes, and the page can say so with a citation rather than as generic Front Range boilerplate.

SLOPE: 0-3%, essentially flat. That is the good news and it distinguishes Twin Lakes from Shaw Heights (same soil, 3-5%) and Todd Creek (worse clay, 3-9%). Flat means no terracing, but it also means water sits — on a smectitic clay subgrade a flat yard is exactly where a poorly built turf base ponds, then the clay swells, then the surface goes wavy.

What to write technically: full sod and topsoil removal down to the clay, geotextile separation over the subgrade, a properly compacted Class 6 / squeegee base with deliberate fall built into the base rather than relying on the existing grade, and perimeter drainage. On the Midtown side, the additional constraint is that courtyard yards are enclosed on three sides by house, fence and alley garage, so there is often nowhere for surface water to go except a designed drain — that is a genuine technical differentiator to write about.

Elevation 5,240 ft. CDP area 4,311 acres, all land per Wikipedia (the gravel ponds and Clear Creek water are outside or excluded).
facts.housing_stock:
