That is a completely different sale from Morrison's hospitality and event turf, from Aspen Park's $30k estate putting green, and from the two canyon CDPs' shade-and-slope story. CANNIBALISATION FLAG: this is the one place in the batch plausibly inside NoCo Turf Co.'s existing northwest-metro coverage (Arvada / Wheat Ridge / north Denver). Check nocoturf.com for an overlapping page before building this one — I could not check it in this session.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Home rule municipality since 1904 with its own municipal code and code enforcement, so the town — not Jefferson County — sets the rules. I could NOT reach tomv.org to read the code, so weed, nuisance, fence, lot-coverage and any front-yard landscape provisions MUST be checked with the town clerk before this page makes any compliance claim. Essentially no HOAs. Colorado SB24-005 applies from 1 Jan 2026 to any commercial, institutional or industrial property and any common-interest-community property in town, barring artificial turf except on athletic fields of play — which matters because the town's commercial strip and its three dispensaries are exactly the properties it covers. Local colour worth knowing: the town once drew 53% of 2014 revenue from police tickets and now takes roughly half its sales tax from three marijuana dispensaries within its twelve blocks.
facts.water_and_rules: THIS IS THE ONE GENUINE GAP — the Town's own site (tomv.org) returned 403/TLS errors throughout this session, so I could not confirm Mountain View's retail water provider from a primary source. Consolidated Mutual Water Company's published boundary (Clear Creek to the north; 32nd Avenue, Pierce Street, Sheridan Boulevard, West Alameda and West 6th Avenue) does NOT reach Mountain View's blocks, which points strongly to Denver Water. VERIFY BY PHONE with the Town before publishing a provider name. What is confirmed and usable either way: Denver Water is in STAGE 1 DROUGHT in 2026 — mandatory outdoor watering two days per week (even addresses Sunday and Thursday, odd addresses Wednesday and Saturday, multifamily and commercial Tuesday and Friday), only before 10 a.m. or after 6 p.m., sprinkler leaks repaired within 10 days, no water reaching pavement, and penalties escalating warning → $250 → $500 → $1,000; and the Denver Board of Water Commissioners has DECLARED AN END TO THE LAWN WATERING SEASON, prohibiting lawn watering and all spray irrigation after 30 September. Consolidated Mutual, serving the adjoining Wheat Ridge and Lakewood blocks, reports moderate-to-severe drought with allowed irrigation ending 1 October 2026. No provider here offers a rebate that artificial turf qualifies for — turf-replacement money funds water-wise living landscape, and SB24-005 now bans artificial turf outright in the commercial and HOA settings those programmes target.
facts.soil_and_yard: Plains and terrace soils east of the Dakota Hogback, on the Denver Formation — THIS is the expansive/swelling-clay belt, unlike the four foothills places in this batch. The Colorado Geological Survey publishes SP-43, a swelling-soils guide for Colorado homebuyers and homeowners, with over 200,000 copies distributed since 1997, precisely because this hazard is endemic to the Front Range urban corridor. Lots are flat, infiltration through clay is poor, and grades run to shallow alley and utility elevations. Base preparation, sub-base drainage and positive slope away from foundations are the whole engineering conversation here — the exact opposite of Kittredge and Aspen Park, where the problem is slope and rock.
facts.housing_stock: A 12-square-block grid platted in 1888 as the Berkeley Annex subdivision on John Brisben Walker's 1879 Berkeley Farm, incorporated as a town on 11 October 1904. Total area 0.093 sq mi with about 272 houses (2008 figure) and a 2020 population of 541 — density 5,800 per square mile, roughly seventeen times any other place in this batch. This is classic Denver Northside stock: narrow pre-war and immediate-post-war lots with 25–50 ft frontages, alleys, detached garages and backyards frequently under 1,000 sq ft, now under heavy scrape-off and pop-top redevelopment spilling west out of Berkeley and Tennyson Street. Elevation 5,384 ft. HOA prevalence effectively zero — a town platted in 1888 and incorporated in 1904, long before covenant communities. CHECK-DATE 2026-09-07.
facts.who_lives_there: DataUSA/ACS: median household income $106,875 (down 1.29% year on year), median property value $596,800 (up 7.69%), homeownership 67.7% — the LOWEST ownership rate in this batch, meaning roughly a third of properties are landlord decisions. Median age 35.2, more than twelve years younger than any other place here and 24 years younger than Morrison. Poverty rate 11.7%. Commute 18.4 minutes; employment up 11% year on year to 342 workers. This is young, urban, dual-income, dog-owning, and it is the one page in the batch where the buyer is price-conscious and comparison-shopping.
facts.golf: Willis Case Golf Course (Denver Parks and Recreation municipal course, 4999 Vrain Street) sits roughly a mile north-east — a public muni, not a country club. No golf community, no private club, no estate golf. Lakeside Amusement Park and Lake Rhoda are immediately north in the Town of Lakeside. Golf is a weak angle here; do not lead with it. A 6x8 backyard chipping green is an upsell, not the pitch.
facts.commercial_targets: Lumberg Elementary School, 6705 West 22nd Avenue, Edgewater 80214 — its own site states it serves Edgewater, MOUNTAIN VIEW and Wheat Ridge, making it the single most defensible named institutional target for this page. Jefferson Junior/Senior High School, 2305 Pierce Street, Edgewater 80214 (the Saints) — the articulation high school. Stevens Elementary School, 7101 West 38th Avenue, Wheat Ridge 80033. Lakeside Amusement Park. The Tennyson Street bar and restaurant patios and dog-friendly taprooms one block east. The Sheridan Boulevard and 44th Avenue commercial strip and the town's three dispensaries. NOTE the SB24-005 constraint: from 1 Jan 2026 those commercial landscape areas are closed — the school athletic fields are the exempt route.
facts.landmarks: Lakeside Amusement Park and Lake Rhoda immediately north in Lakeside — opened 1908, nicknamed "White City", founded by a syndicate led by Denver brewer Adolph Zang. The Walmart and strip retail on the site of the former 1956 Lakeside Center mall. The Tennyson Street Cultural District, with its monthly Art Walks, one block east in Denver's Berkeley neighbourhood. Berkeley Lake Park and Rocky Mountain Lake Park. Willis Case Golf Course. Crown Hill Park to the west. Town Hall on Benton Street. Bounded by Lakeside north, Wheat Ridge west and south, Denver east.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH SHADE AND SLOPE, NOT WATER. Kittredge is a 7,074-ft north-side canyon town where real grass has never worked — not because of drought, but because of ponderosa and Douglas-fir shade, pine litter, elk browse, snow cover into spring and a growing season measured in weeks. The page should open with "grass doesn't grow in Bear Creek Canyon" and sell the terraced, level play pad or putting green carved out of a hillside, engineered to drain away from the creek. That is deliberately the OPPOSITE of the Mountain View page (which leads with Denver Water restrictions and a 25-ft city lot) and different from Morrison next door (which leads with visitor traffic, the historic district and Morrison-Formation expansive clay). Secondary hooks: affluent, 85%+ owner-occupied, and a private backyard green for the Hiwan/Evergreen golfer who does not want to drive down the canyon.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Jefferson County unincorporated zoning governs; there is no municipal turf ordinance. Two rules that actually bite: (1) Colorado SB24-005, signed 7 Aug 2024, prohibits installing nonfunctional turf, ARTIFICIAL TURF and invasive plant species on commercial, institutional and industrial property, common-interest-community (HOA) property, and street rights-of-way / parking lots / medians / transportation corridors — local governments from 1 Jan 2026, state facilities from 1 Jan 2025 — with artificial turf on athletic fields of play expressly exempted. Single-family residential yards are not covered. (2) Wildfire defensible space: this is Jefferson County WUI, and Zone 1 (0–5 ft from the structure) guidance discourages combustible material against the house — relevant to where turf can be laid. Essentially no HOA covenants to work around.
facts.water_and_rules: Unincorporated — NO municipal water utility. I could NOT confirm a public water district for Kittredge from an authoritative source in this session (the likely Kittredge Sanitation and Water District has no reachable public site; the Special District Association directory and EPA SDWIS were both unreachable). The practical situation in this stretch of Bear Creek Canyon is individual permitted wells and small shared systems; Evergreen Metropolitan District's confirmed service area is Evergreen, and Indian Hills has its own Indian Hills Water District — neither covers Kittredge. VERIFY BY PHONE before this goes on a page. Consequently: no municipal watering-restriction schedule to cite, and no turf rebate. Statewide, Colorado's turf-replacement incentives fund water-wise LIVING landscape; artificial turf is not an eligible replacement, and SB24-005 now prohibits artificial turf outright in the commercial/HOA settings those rebates target. Denver Water's Stage 1 drought rules (2 days/week, nothing after Sept 30, 2026) do NOT apply here — do not borrow that argument for this page.
facts.soil_and_yard: Precambrian crystalline bedrock (granite/gneiss) with thin, gravelly, fast-draining decomposed-granite soils, acidic under conifer litter. Expansive clay is NOT the local problem — swelling soils are a hogback-and-plains hazard (Morrison Formation bentonitic mudstone, Pierre Shale, Denver Formation), and Kittredge sits well west of the Dakota Hogback. The real constraints are slope, shallow bedrock that defeats deep excavation, pine-needle litter, snow load and a short growing season at 7,074 ft. Flood is the live hazard: the CDP sits in the valley of Bear Creek, and the WPA built masonry flood-control walls along SH 74 through this canyon. Base design here is terracing, retention and drainage away from the creek, not clay mitigation.
facts.housing_stock: Origin is a 1920s Denver summer-cabin colony strung along Bear Creek — the Kittredge post office has run since 1923, and the neighbouring Indian Hills CDP documents the identical pattern of "small lots sold to Denver residents seeking summer homes in the mountains" from the 1920s. The stock today is those cabins winterized and expanded from roughly the 1960s through the 1990s, plus scattered custom mountain homes. 2020 census: 582 housing units, 9.1% vacant, 529 households, across 1.884 sq mi at 7,074 ft. Lots are small by mountain standards, steep, creek-adjacent and heavily treed; usable flat backyard is often only 300–1,200 sq ft on a bench cut into the slope. HOA prevalence is near zero — this is unincorporated county with no master-planned subdivisions. CHECK-DATE 2026-09-07. CAVEAT: ACS-derived figures for a CDP this small are unstable — DataUSA reports population 812 and median age 57.2 against the 2020 census 1,308 and median age 41.2. Use the decennial figures for population and treat income as directional only.
facts.who_lives_there: 53.5% married-couple households; census median age 41.2 (ACS says 57.2 — wide disagreement, small-sample noise). 90.7% White, 4.8% Hispanic/Latino. DataUSA/ACS 2024: median household income $222,500 (up 48.6% in one year — treat as unreliable but clearly affluent), median property value $744,000, homeownership 85.7%. Former U.S. Senator Gary Hart lives in Kittredge. Practically: Denver-commuting professionals and semi-retired mountain-lifestyle owners who chose the canyon deliberately and have already spent money on the house.
facts.golf: No course in Kittredge. Hiwan Golf Club, Evergreen — private, opened 1962, Press Maxwell design, par 70, 7,097 yards, Colorado Open host 1964–1991, Bergen Peak visible from nearly every hole — is roughly 6 miles west. Evergreen Golf Course (City and County of Denver municipal course, at Evergreen Lake) is roughly 5 miles west. Red Rocks Country Club, private, in Jefferson County just outside Morrison, is roughly 10 miles east down Bear Creek Canyon. There is no golf community in Kittredge itself — the golf angle here is a private backyard green for members who play at Hiwan or Evergreen.
facts.commercial_targets: Thin — be honest on the page. Parmalee Elementary School, 4460 Parmalee Gulch Road, Indian Hills 80454 (the Bear Creek/Indian Hills feeder). Red Rocks Elementary School, 17199 Highway 74, Morrison 80465 — the Bear Creek articulation elementary, downstream in the canyon. Kittredge Park ballfield. Canyon taverns and cafés with creekside patios on SH 74. Six miles west in Evergreen: Wilmot, Bergen Meadow and Bergen Valley elementaries, Evergreen Middle and High, and Hiwan Golf Club. Under SB24-005 the only clean commercial play from 2026 is athletic fields of play.
facts.landmarks: Bear Creek; Kittredge Park; State Highway 74 through town is the Bear Creek Canyon Scenic Mountain Drive, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, with WPA masonry flood walls along the creek; Lair o' the Bear Park (Jefferson County Open Space, on SH 74 between Idledale and Kittredge — location not re-confirmed from a live source this session, verify); Corwina Park, O'Fallon Park and Pence Park (Denver Mountain Parks in this canyon); 8 miles east to Morrison, 2 miles to Evergreen. Gary Hart is the town's best-known resident.

facts.strongest_angle: THE YARD THE MOWER CANNOT REACH — smallest, steepest, shadiest and most flood-marked lots in the batch, on the cheapest houses. Idledale's job is a 300–800 sq ft postage stamp on a slope above Bear Creek: a small level pad, a dog area, terraced steps, engineered to drain safely toward a creek that washed the town off the map in 1933. Lead with that specific, physical picture and with the 1933 Starbuck Heights story, which every resident knows and no competitor will use. That is deliberately distinct from Kittredge four miles upstream (bigger lots, far more money, shade-and-elk lead), from Morrison four miles downstream (visitor traffic, historic district, hogback clay) and from Mountain View (water restrictions, city lot, pets). HONEST STRATEGIC NOTE FOR THE CLIENT: with 244 residents and a $451,900 median home value, this is the weakest of the five pages commercially. Build it lean — enough to capture "Bear Creek Canyon" and "80453" searches and to internally support the Morrison and Kittredge pages — and do not invest estate-tier design here.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Jefferson County unincorporated zoning; no municipal ordinance of any kind because there is no municipality. The live constraints are (1) Bear Creek floodplain regulation — the binding rule for most Idledale lots, and worth naming explicitly; (2) SH 74 through Idledale is the Bear Creek Canyon Scenic Mountain Drive, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, so anything in or visibly affecting the highway right-of-way is sensitive; (3) Jefferson County WUI wildfire defensible-space guidance, which discourages combustible material in Zone 1 within 0–5 ft of structures; and (4) Colorado SB24-005 from 1 Jan 2026, prohibiting artificial turf on commercial, institutional, industrial and common-interest-community property and in rights-of-way, with athletic fields of play exempt. Effectively no HOA covenants.
facts.water_and_rules: No municipal water utility — unincorporated Jefferson County with no town government. I could NOT confirm any public water district for Idledale from an authoritative source in this session (the Special District Association directory, EPA SDWIS and the Bear Creek Watershed Association site were all unreachable). Neighbouring Indian Hills has the Indian Hills Water District and Evergreen has the Evergreen Metropolitan District, but neither covers Idledale. The practical situation in this stretch of canyon is private wells and small shared systems. VERIFY BY PHONE before publishing any provider name. Consequently: no watering-restriction schedule to cite, no rebate, and Denver Water's Stage 1 rules do NOT apply — do not borrow them. Colorado's turf-replacement incentives fund living water-wise landscape, not artificial turf.
facts.soil_and_yard: Bear Creek Canyon conditions: thin, rocky soils over Precambrian crystalline bedrock, steep north-side slopes falling to the creek, and shallow bedrock that limits excavation depth. Expansive clay is not the local problem — that is a hogback and plains hazard, and Idledale sits west of it. FLOOD IS THE DEFINING HAZARD: the town was nearly destroyed by a storm in 1933 and renamed on rebuild, and the WPA built masonry flood-control walls along SH 74 through this canyon to protect the roadway. Deep canyon-wall and conifer shade means natural turf genuinely fails here regardless of irrigation. Any installation must be engineered for drainage and for creek setbacks, and that should be stated openly on the page.
facts.housing_stock: The smallest footprint in the batch by a wide margin: 0.277 square miles — 177 acres total — holding a 2020 population of 244 at a density of 881 per square mile and an elevation of 6,598 ft, on the north side of Bear Creek along SH 74. Originally platted as STARBUCK HEIGHTS, the town was almost washed out by a storm in 1933 and was renamed Idledale when it was rebuilt — so the stock is 1920s Denver summer-cabin construction, rebuilt post-1933, winterized piecemeal since. Lots are measured in thousands of square feet, not acres: tiny, steep, stacked on the canyon wall above the creek. Homeownership 80.3%. Essentially no HOAs and no subdivision covenants. Population is flat to declining (252 in 2010 → 244 in 2020). CHECK-DATE 2026-09-07. HONEST NOTE: this is the thinnest place in the batch and the research is genuinely limited — there is no town government, no chamber, and no local data beyond the census.
facts.who_lives_there: DataUSA/ACS: median household income $122,841 (2020), median property value $451,900 (2024) — the LOWEST home value in this batch by roughly $240,000 and less than half Morrison's $875,000 — homeownership 80.3%, reported population 297. Predominantly White non-Hispanic. The profile is solid income against modest housing: Denver-commuting owners who bought into the canyon for the location and the price, not for acreage. That gap between income and home value is the single most useful commercial fact on this page — these are people with money to spend on a yard they cannot expand.
facts.golf: None in Idledale, and none nearby. Red Rocks Country Club, private, outside Morrison, is roughly 6 miles east down the canyon. Evergreen Golf Course (City of Denver) and Hiwan Golf Club (private, Evergreen) are roughly 8–10 miles west. Golf is a weak angle for Idledale — there is not enough flat ground for a meaningful backyard green on most lots. Do not lead with it.
facts.commercial_targets: Very few, and the page should say so rather than pad. Red Rocks Elementary School, 17199 Highway 74, Morrison 80465 — the Bear Creek articulation elementary, the closest institutional client and, under SB24-005, viable only for athletic-field work. Parmalee Elementary, 4460 Parmalee Gulch Road, Indian Hills 80454. The handful of canyon cafés and taverns on SH 74. Denver Mountain Parks picnic grounds at Corwina, O'Fallon and Pence. Realistically this should be built as a purely residential page.
facts.landmarks: Bear Creek and the Bear Creek Canyon Scenic Mountain Drive (SH 74, National Register-listed), with WPA masonry flood walls along the creek. Lair o' the Bear Park, Jefferson County Open Space, on SH 74 between Idledale and Kittredge — well known locally but NOT re-confirmed from a live source this session, so verify. Corwina Park, O'Fallon Park and Pence Park, all Denver Mountain Parks in this canyon. Approximately 4 miles downstream to Morrison and 4 miles upstream to Kittredge. Red Rocks Elementary at 17199 Highway 74 sits just down-canyon. The Starbuck Heights name and the 1933 flood are the local-history hooks a resident will recognise instantly.

facts.strongest_angle: THE PRIVATE PUTTING GREEN AT 8,000 FEET, ON A WELL, WITH NO COURSE WITHIN ELEVEN MILES. This is the only place in the batch where the lead is not water restrictions and not lawn replacement — because there are few lawns and no municipal restrictions. It is high-income, 97% owner-occupied, 26.4% work-from-home, large-acreage households whose water likely comes from a permit that forbids lawn irrigation and whose nearest golf is a 25-minute drive down CO-73. Lead with the backyard putting green, then the dog run and the level, mud-free, elk-proof play pad cut into a treed slope. This is a premium, low-volume, high-ticket page aimed squarely at the client's $10–12/sq ft ambition — the opposite of Mountain View's dense, price-sensitive city-lot page and of Idledale's postage-stamp work. Secondary: honest wildfire-defensible-space guidance, which competitors in the 285 corridor will not put in writing.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Jefferson County unincorporated zoning; no municipal turf ordinance. The de facto landscape rulebook here is WILDFIRE, not water: Aspen Park sits in the Elk Creek Fire Protection District, and defensible-space Zone 1 (0–5 ft from structures) guidance discourages combustible material against the house — this governs where turf can go and should be addressed head-on rather than avoided. Colorado SB24-005 (signed 7 Aug 2024) prohibits artificial turf on commercial, institutional and industrial property, common-interest-community property and street rights-of-way from 1 Jan 2026 for local governments, EXEMPTING artificial turf on athletic fields of play — so subdivision common areas are closed to this client from 2026 while school fields stay open. Individual subdivision covenants vary and should be checked per job.
facts.water_and_rules: No municipal water supply. Aspen Park Metropolitan District is named as the service provider for the CDP (Wikipedia), but I could NOT reach any district site to confirm whether it supplies potable water, sewer, or only roads — VERIFY BY PHONE. The residential norm across this part of mountain Jefferson County is individual permitted wells. IMPORTANT AND UNVERIFIED: Colorado exempt well permits are use-limited, and a "household use only" permit does not authorise lawn or landscape irrigation, while permits allowing up to one acre of lawn and garden generally require 35+ acres. If that holds for Aspen Park parcels it is the decisive economic argument on this page — but the Colorado Division of Water Resources page returned 403 in this session, so it MUST be confirmed with DWR before it becomes copy. There is no municipal watering-restriction schedule to cite and no local turf rebate; Denver Water's Stage 1 drought rules do NOT apply here.
facts.soil_and_yard: 8,000-ft granitic and gneissic mountain soils — thin, gravelly, acidic under heavy conifer canopy, fast-draining but erosion-prone on cut slopes where sheet flow concentrates. No expansive-clay issue (that is a hogback and plains problem, not an 8,000-ft Front Range foothills one). The governing conditions are steep decomposed-granite grades, frost heave, a six-to-eight month frozen and snow-covered season, and constant elk and mule deer traffic that shreds and compacts natural turf. Yards are large on paper and tiny in practice — the buildable, level, sunny fraction of a 2-acre treed lot at 8,091 ft is small.
facts.housing_stock: 1970s–2000s custom mountain homes on large treed acreages at 8,091 ft. 2020 population 810 across 2.486 sq mi — a density of 330 per square mile, i.e. most parcels are 1–5+ acres and the CDP is essentially a low-density forested subdivision belt straddling US 285 at the headwaters of South Turkey Creek, with North Turkey Creek forming the western boundary. Homeownership is 97% — effectively no rental market. Population has DECLINED 8.2% since 2010 (882 → 810), so this is a stable, aging, built-out place, not a growth market. Backyards are large but rarely flat: usable turf areas are cut pads, not lawns. HOA prevalence is limited to individual subdivision covenant associations; Wikipedia records that an Aspen Park Metropolitan District provides services, but I could NOT confirm from a public source what services it actually delivers — verify. CHECK-DATE 2026-09-07.
facts.who_lives_there: DataUSA/ACS: median household income $104,167 (down slightly year on year), median property value $693,100, homeownership 97%, median age 47.3, 86.4% White non-Hispanic. Workforce of 277: educational services (64), professional/scientific/technical (63), retail (51). 26.4% work from home — unusually high, and the single most useful fact on this page: these are people who are at home looking at their yard all day. Male median earnings $141,635 vs female $59,423. Average 2 cars per household, 22.3-minute commute.
facts.golf: THERE IS NO GOLF COURSE IN ASPEN PARK OR CONIFER — and that absence is the pitch. Nearest are Hiwan Golf Club (private, Evergreen, 1962, Press Maxwell, par 70, 7,097 yds) and Evergreen Golf Course (City of Denver municipal, at Evergreen Lake), both roughly 11–12 miles north via CO-73. Red Rocks Country Club is far down the hill outside Morrison. Aspen Park is backyard-putting-green territory, not golf-community territory.
facts.commercial_targets: Conifer High School, 10441 Highway 73, Conifer 80433 — 105-acre campus, 819 students (2024-25), the Lobos, serving Conifer, Aspen Park and Bailey. Its athletic fields are the single best commercial target in this batch because SB24-005 expressly exempts artificial turf on fields of play. Marshdale Elementary School, 26663 North Turkey Creek Road, Evergreen 80439 (Conifer articulation area — and North Turkey Creek is Aspen Park's own western boundary). West Jefferson Elementary and West Jefferson Middle School in Conifer (addresses not confirmed this session). Elk Creek Fire Protection District stations. The Aspen Park commercial strip on US 285. Honest assessment: outside the schools, this is a very thin commercial market and the page should not pretend otherwise.
facts.landmarks: The US 285 / CO-73 junction at Aspen Park is the commercial heart of the mountain 285 corridor. Meyer Ranch Park (Jefferson County Open Space) is on US 285 at Aspen Park — widely known locally, but I could NOT re-confirm it from a live source this session, so verify before publishing. Staunton State Park (3,908 acres) is 6 miles west. The Conifer Junction Schoolhouse and the 1889 Midway House are the recognised historic structures. Beaver Ranch Park is in Conifer. South Turkey Creek and North Turkey Creek define the CDP.
